# Cohort 88: nested journey global chronology and construction

The three-level connect journey's final raw reads consume a fixed eventrecord
chronology projection through the original selected read coordinator. All events
remain visible across runs, with ascending created_at/event_id ties, original
entity/flow COALESCE defaults and exact diagnostic rendering. The name-only
witness derives its same ordered names from those detached rows; no timestamp
cutoff, run/name/status filter, limit or eligibility reconstruction is introduced.

The old diagnostic's silent query/scan failures are removed in favor of explicit
fail-closed observation. Read/scan/iteration/close failure returns no partial
rows. With no remaining pool use, the same native PostgreSQL fixture constructor
owns setup and cleanup rather than a raw harness and reconstructed coordinator.

The existing whole-root codemod is reconciled, not duplicated. Its oracle
normalizes only the two exact read substitutions and native constructor. Fixed
SQL/column/order and no-raw-consumption guards accompany the actual unchanged
PG end-to-end root under race. Independent SQLite/PostgreSQL controls insert
different runs out of order, retain nonempty entity/flow metadata, prove tied-ID
ordering and one original read/no writes, then reject cancelled/closed/missing
authority without partial evidence.

This closes this journey's raw storage tail, not the remaining neighboring
nested-routing or global fixture classes. Existing broad #2542 approval and
raw_sql_policy govern; no runtime semantics/spec, framework, compatibility,
architecture or tracker change is introduced.
